LESSON: WEAVING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Creating and Executing
Topic 1.5: Weaving

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Weaving. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is recycling beneficial to the environment?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify a plain weave for familiarity
2. appreciate our own and peers’ woven items used for gymnastics performance

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WEAVING
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Weaving helps you succeed in CREATIVE ARTS. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: WEAVING
Study Weaving like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify a plain weave for familiarity

What this means
In this part you learn to identify a plain weave for familiarity. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify a plain weave for familiarity.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Weaving” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify a plain weave for familiarity. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate our own and peers’ woven items used for gymnastics performance

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate our own and peers’ woven items used for gymnastics performance. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate our own and peers’ woven items used for gymnastics performance.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Weaving in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate our own and peers’ woven items used for gymnastics performance. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Weaving is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Weaving” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: identify a plain weave for familiarity)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Weaving in your own words. (skill: appreciate our own and peers’ woven items used for gymnastics performance)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Weaving to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify a plain weave for familiarity.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate our own and peers’ woven items used for gymnastics performance.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Weaving from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Weaving: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Weaving?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is recycling beneficial to the environment?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Weaving means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify a plain weave for familiarity.
5. Be able to: appreciate our own and peers’ woven items used for gymnastics performance.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
